summary: You is a point at the person you're talking to. For a group, sweep the point across them in an arc.
steps: Point your index finger at the person.
For 'you all,' sweep the point across the group.
Keep eye contact. In ASL pointing at someone is normal grammar, not rude.
mistakes: Pointing vaguely into the air. Point at the person, or at the spot you've set up for them.

faq.q: Is pointing at someone rude in ASL?
faq.a: No. Pointing is how ASL does pronouns. It's expected and polite.
